title: The greater dog from Paranal
caption: Sirius and Canopus over the road to Cerro Paranal, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A winding road climbs toward Cerro Paranal under a starry sky. Near the top left of the picture shines Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky. The road leads up to ESO's Very Large Telescope.

Sirius belongs to the constellation Canis Major, the Greater Dog, where it marks the animal's neck. Other stars of the constellation appear as well. The dog's head lies to the left of Sirius, and three nearly aligned stars to its right trace a hind leg.

Over in the right part of the image is another bright star, Canopus, which belongs to Carina, the Keel. Constellations are patterns that people have drawn among stars that usually lie at very different distances from us, so the shape of the dog is a matter of perspective rather than a physical grouping.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera near Paranal. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: Sirius and Canopus are easy to see with the naked eye, but a long exposure collects more light and reveals many fainter stars around them.

explore: The photograph gives a human-scale view of Paranal, showing the winding road up to Cerro Paranal, where the Very Large Telescope stands, rather than the telescopes themselves.
alt: A winding road beneath a starry sky, with the bright star Sirius near the top left and Canopus on the right.
